Q: Lua Relational Operators with multiple condition A: 
a = nil
b = nil
c = nil
if b == c == a ~= nil then
  1. (b == c) means nil == nil, so true
  2. (b == c) == a means true == nil, so false
  3. (b == c) ~= a means true ~= nil, so true

Q: How to write automation tests for elements/processes that are frequently used elsewhere? A:

One of the simple approaches is using a headless browser. For example, if you want to use h5i browser, you can write a script like:

h5i browser open https://automationintesting.online/ \
  --session calendar-test \
  --new \
  --script

# obtain current @ref handles.
h5i browser snapshot --session calendar-test

# (alternative option) locate the field by its accessible role and name.
h5i browser find \
  --session calendar-test \
  --role textbox \
  --name "Check in"

# use the @ref returned by snapshot/find.
h5i browser click @e7 --session calendar-test

# opening the calendar changes the DOM, and take a screenshot
h5i browser snapshot --delta --session calendar-test

# use the new refs to navigate the calendar and select a day.
h5i browser click @e12 --session calendar-test
h5i browser snapshot --delta --session calendar-test
h5i browser click @e23 --session calendar-test

# read the resulting state for an assertion in the surrounding test.
result="$(
  h5i browser extract \
    '{"check_in":{"selector":".col-md-6:nth-child(1) .dateWrapper input","attr":"value"}}' \
    --json \
    --session calendar-test
)"

Then, you can extract the actual value with something like actual_date="$(jq -er '.data.check_in' <<<"$result")", and compare it with the expected date.

Q: Git add and commit in one command A:

Here is a sample on how to get a useful git add + git commit in one go with explicit files and paths including several -m options. Add it in your ~/.gitconfig. It uses bash's vector feature to reduce complexity. Enjoy.

This post was inspired by Git add and commit in one command by Positive Navid

[alias]
    # This alias is a short for git add and git commit
    # usage: git ac -m "comment1" -m "comment2" [--dry-run] ./file1 ./file2
    ac = "!bash -c 'msgs=(); flags=(); files=(); while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do case \"$1\" in -m) msgs+=(\"-m\" \"$2\"); shift 2;; --dry-run) flags+=(\"--dry-run\"); shift;; *) files+=(\"$1\"); shift;; esac; done; git a
dd \"${files[@]}\" && git commit \"${flags[@]}\" \"${msgs[@]}\"' _"

Q: How to create a smooth sliding overlay sidebar in CSS without layout jitter and unwanted horizontal scrollbar? A:

Using transform: translateX() instead of animating width should avoid reflow, while overflow-x: hidden can prevent the unwanted scrollbar.

Q: SQL Server driver which could not establish a secure connection by using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)? A:

I had this issue recently, it was because I was trying to connect to an old version of Microsoft SQL Server (2012, ver. 11.00.3156) using the latest version of the SQL Server JDBC Driver (ver. 12.2.0) with a newer version JDK (ver. 11.0.15).

It happens because newer version of JDK by default disable some old security algorithms like TLSv1.0 (in favor of newer like TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3) which the old SQL Server is requiring as security algorithm.

To solve the issue I changed the JDBC driver to an older version 8.2.2 and I had to pass some java security VM options to the JDK to override some security configs and remove TLSV1.0 from the disabled algorithms

VM options to pass to JDK

-Djdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms=SSLv3, RC4, DES, MD5withRSA, DH keySize < 1024, EC keySize < 224, 3DES_EDE_CBC, anon, NULL

(note that TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 are removed from the original JDK list)

Doing that I managed to successfully connect to the old SQL Server 2012. Hope this help you

Q: javax.validation.ConstraintViolationException, ConstraintViolationImpl{interpolatedMessage='may not be null', propertyPath= A:

On AngularJS side, ngInit is not recommended. Try to set the value in the controller and only use ngModel. Display it with {{}} to be sure, and inspect the request to double check when saving. On java side, run in debug mode to see if something is received and why nothing is populated in workflow. Obviously, it's null according to the validation error.

Q: How to align centre a custom label in highcharts A:

If you wish, you could also add an HTML element after the chart has been generated to do this effect (see example at http://jsfiddle.net/brightmatrix/5517s8zb/1/).

In this case, to get the proper centered effect, you'll need to explicitly define the container div's width.

<div id="container" style="height: 400px; width: 100%"></div>

Here is the HTML element:

/* add an HTML element to the chart starting at 0px from the left corner and 
   10% of the container's height from the top */
chart.renderer.html('<div align="center" style="font-size: 20px; width: ' + 
$('#container').width() + 'px">Center Me!</div>',0,$('#container').height()*.1).add();

I did the 10% of the container's height to help make the position more flexible. You could also choose to add or subtract specific pixel dimensions until you get it placed where you like.

I hope this is helpful!
